groups.title: An agent that stays with the work
groups.description: From the first question to the next change, keep context, decisions, and activity together.

groups.title: A clear view of your project
groups.description: A native desktop built around conversation, inspection, and the moments that need your attention.

groups.title: Bring the right context and tools
groups.description: Connect model providers, project knowledge, and external tools without losing the thread.

groups.title: Take the same agent into your workflow
groups.description: Use native commands for one-shot work or embed the Rust agent in your own host.

groups.title: Reach beyond the project files
groups.description: Optional browser, computer, and mobile capabilities, with their current availability made explicit.

groups.title: Installation and maintenance
groups.description: Packaging and update infrastructure are implemented, with release verification still in progress.

groups.title: Built in the open
groups.description: The supporting tools and public surfaces behind SunCode. These are separate from the agent's runtime.

features.title: Project-aware conversations
features.description: Open a project and work through persistent sessions with streamed responses, visible tool activity, and cancellation.
details: Queue follow-up messages or steer the next model request while work continues.
Use project instructions, local Skills, structured questions, todos, and model-supported image attachments.
features.note: Queued follow-ups stay in memory until admitted to conversation history. Model requests send selected context to your configured provider.

features.title: Long-session context
features.description: Continue longer conversations with automatic, model-assisted context compaction and context-overflow recovery.
details: Preserves complete tool-call groups and a recent conversation tail.
Keeps a structured summary of decisions, pending requests, and verification state.
features.note: Compaction is a bounded summary; it does not promise unlimited or lossless memory.

features.title: Six specialist agents
features.description: Let the primary agent delegate focused work to Architect, UI/UX, Product, Software Engineering, QA, and SRE specialists.
details: Inspect linked child sessions and resolve their operation approvals.
Each role has a restricted tool set and uses the same Rust policy and audit paths.
features.note: Roles are fixed. Specialists cannot delegate again, use MCP, or ask questions. Child checkpoints remain separate from parent-turn undo.

features.title: Scoped actions and file undo
features.description: Search, read, and edit project files, run commands, and retrieve web text through audited Rust operations.
details: Approve sensitive operations with their scope visible; inspect tool results and artifacts.
Restore checkpointed file mutations with checks for conflicting changes.
features.note: Shell, Terminal, MCP, browser, and computer effects are outside filesystem undo. Policy and the dispatcher are not an OS sandbox.

features.title: Native desktop workbench
features.description: Move between projects, conversations, read-only files, tool activity, approvals, and checkpoint review in a .NET 10 Avalonia interface.
details: Restore project windows, pin and archive sessions, and inspect read-only system Git status and diffs.
Choose light or dark appearance and English or Simplified Chinese.
features.note: The file viewer is read-only. The changed-file panel currently combines paths across the session; Git review shows the current repository, not a historical per-turn diff.

features.title: Markdown, math, and diagrams
features.description: Read formatted responses with mathematical formulas, Mermaid diagrams, code blocks, and copyable source.
details: Diagrams adapt to the application theme and offer pan, zoom, and source disclosure.
Incomplete or unsupported syntax retains a readable source fallback.
features.note: Windows ARM64 math falls back to source. Installed macOS/Linux native rendering still needs release verification; full TeX or Mermaid.js parity is not promised.

features.title: Independent shells and terminal tabs
features.description: Choose Agent and interactive Terminal shells independently, with local terminal tabs that start in your project.
details: Detect custom shell paths and reuse an existing PowerShell 7 installation.
Windows can explicitly download and verify a pinned PowerShell runtime when needed.
features.note: Terminal sessions use your normal user authority and are outside Agent approvals and undo. Official PowerShell setup and broader platform conformance remain under verification.

features.title: Provider transfer activity
features.description: See current provider upload and download rates in the desktop footer, with active model and byte totals in the tooltip.
details: Rates update during model exchanges and clear when sessions change.
Transient traffic samples stay out of persisted provider traces.
features.note: Rates measure provider HTTP body bytes, not device bandwidth or network-protocol overhead.

features.title: Attention when you need it
features.description: Receive desktop notifications when background work completes, fails, or needs an approval or answer.
details: Notification text omits prompts, responses, paths, and tool data.
Activation returns to the relevant session or child approval.
features.note: Installed notification display and click behavior still need verification on macOS, Windows, GNOME, and KDE. Mobile push is not implemented.

features.title: Redacted diagnostics
features.description: Inspect separate rotating agent and desktop logs, with configurable detail, location, size, and retention.
details: Failures include safe operation and session correlation where available.
Credentials, prompts, model output, file contents, and screenshot bytes are excluded from diagnostic logs.
features.note: Diagnostic logs are separate from local conversation history and provider-trace inspection.

features.title: Model and provider choice
features.description: Choose from the seeded provider catalog, manage provider credentials, and configure existing provider endpoints.
details: Select model-advertised capabilities and reasoning options.
Provider keys default to the operating-system credential store, with an explicit plaintext option.
features.note: Capabilities and access depend on the model and provider account. Catalog entries are not a guarantee of live compatibility; arbitrary provider/model creation is not available in the client.

features.title: MCP tool connections
features.description: Connect local stdio and remote Streamable HTTP MCP servers, and manage them from desktop Settings.
details: Load project connections in the background while built-in tools remain usable.
Edit, enable, retry, or remove servers without restarting a conversation.
features.note: Tools only: MCP prompts, resources, and OAuth are not implemented. Local servers run with user authority; their side effects are outside undo.

features.title: Language-aware project context
features.description: Give the agent diagnostics, definitions, references, hover information, and symbols from project-scoped language servers.
details: Configure jdtls, vtsls, basedpyright, rust-analyzer, and Roslyn integrations.
Keep server processes and document state separate for each project.
features.note: Install the servers and language toolchains locally. The current catalog is fixed and supports read-only queries, not completion, formatting, or code actions.

features.title: PDF and Office document context
features.description: Inspect, read, and search PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and OpenDocument Spreadsheet content with bounded extraction tools.
details: Read pages, slides, Word blocks, and typed spreadsheet cell ranges.
Use extracted text and available formulas as context without opening an Office application.
features.note: DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODS, and targeted PDF cases have fixtures. Legacy DOC/PPT/XLS adapters need representative binary verification. No OCR, document editing, or formula recalculation.

features.title: Network configuration
features.description: Configure certificate trust and no-proxy, system-proxy, or custom HTTP/HTTPS proxy modes.
details: Add custom trust roots and proxy bypass rules.
Built-in providers, web retrieval, remote MCP, and relay transport use the shared network configuration.
features.note: Coverage varies by client: CEF uses host networking, component updates retain strict trust, and external processes control their own traffic. A separate developer proxy can inspect API exchanges.

features.title: Native command-line tools
features.description: Use the Rust CLI to inspect runtime health, list models, manage credentials, and read configuration.
details: Choose readable text or versioned JSONL output.
Use isolated data paths and explicit host configuration for scripts.
features.note: The CLI and desktop cannot simultaneously own the same data directory. Interactive chat and approval/question prompts are not implemented.

features.title: One-shot agent runs
features.description: Submit one project turn from a command-line prompt or stdin, and consume final text or streamed JSONL events.
details: Uses the same embedded Rust agent, policy, and tool boundary.
Supports model overrides and interrupt-driven cancellation.
features.note: A turn waiting for an approval or question exits with status 4. Browser Use and Computer Use are disabled in the CLI.

features.title: Continue a saved session
features.description: Submit one new turn to a saved primary session while reusing its durable conversation context.
details: Reopens an archived session when appropriate.
Shares event streaming, cancellation, and lag recovery with one-shot runs.
features.note: Pending approvals and questions must be resolved elsewhere; resume fails closed rather than bypassing them.

features.title: Session administration
features.description: List a project's primary sessions, including archived records, or archive a session through native commands.
details: Returns stable session identities and SDK-projected state.
Uses typed SDK lifecycle methods for ownership and state validation.
features.note: This provides list/archive operations, not an interactive session browser or full terminal UI.

features.title: An embeddable Rust SDK
features.description: Embed the agent through an async-first Rust facade or an explicit blocking adapter, with C and C# bindings used by the desktop.
details: Receive typed event streams and atomic session snapshots with subscriptions.
Restrict host capabilities and explicitly shut down runtime-owned resources.
features.note: Python and TypeScript bindings are placeholders. No remote agent service or published package availability is implied.

features.title: Local session persistence
features.description: Keep conversations, settings, approvals, checkpoints, and recovery state in Rust-owned local SQLite storage.
details: Recover interrupted work without blindly replaying operations.
Clients use the SDK instead of accessing the database directly.
features.note: Local state does not mean offline inference. Selected context still reaches configured model providers, and some explicitly configured secrets can be stored as plaintext.

features.title: Browser Use and local preview
features.description: Use optional CEF-enabled desktop builds to navigate and interact with web pages or preview a local development server.
details: Browser actions use Rust-owned CDP tools and project-isolated profiles.
Each Browser Use call requires interactive approval, including under Full Control.
features.note: CEF is excluded from default builds and baseline installers. Preview is partial; screenshot images do not reach the model, and Windows/Linux packaging checks remain open.

features.title: Computer Use
features.description: An optional Rust capability observes the primary display and provides approved desktop input, screenshot, and accessibility tools.
details: Exclusive control, user takeover, held-input cleanup, and emergency stop.
Provider-neutral tools for models supporting vision and multimodal tool results.
features.note: Partial implementation, off by default. Approval-continuation semantics and platform conformance remain incomplete. Wayland, multi-display control, and secure desktops are not supported.

features.title: Paired remote control
features.description: Connect a desktop to a relay through an outbound connection so a paired companion can drive its sessions.
details: Forward scoped messages, cancellation, approvals, and answers through local Rust authority.
Optional AES-256-GCM payload encryption is enabled by default; routing metadata remains visible to the relay.
features.note: Cross-component conformance and desktop token refresh remain open. Relay state is in memory, so a server restart requires re-pairing.

features.title: A mobile companion
features.description: Pair an Android or iOS companion to browse projects, follow a session, send text, and respond to approvals and questions.
details: QR pairing, platform credential storage, offline cache, and reconnecting live updates.
English and Simplified Chinese layouts for phone and tablet.
features.note: Android has focused tests; iOS compiles but device behavior and native scanners need verification. Desktop and relay must be available. No image sending, background delivery, or push notifications.

features.title: Windows offline installation
features.description: Build a current-user offline installer bundling the desktop, .NET runtime, and matching Rust SDK.
details: Standard shortcuts, activation, uninstall, and same-version repair.
Uninstall preserves application data and unrelated files.
features.note: x64 build and isolated lifecycle checks pass. Signing, clean-machine checks, ARM64, and managed-update enrollment remain unverified. CEF and CLI are excluded.

features.title: macOS and Linux packaging
features.description: Build a macOS app/DMG or Linux Debian and portable archives from native packaging scripts.
details: macOS supports optional Developer ID signing and notarization.
Linux supports desktop integration through Debian or an unregistered portable launcher.
features.note: Native reruns, installed behavior, and release signing remain under verification. Packaging source does not establish downloadable signed releases. CEF and CLI are excluded.

features.title: Independent component updates
features.description: Check signed metadata and plan compatible desktop and SDK updates independently, with staged verification and explicit restart.
details: Update checking and SDK repair remain accessible when agent startup fails.
Verify archive identities, compatibility, and durable paired activation before changing the selected runtime.
features.note: Catalog checking is enabled, but current catalog archive values are samples. Real packages, signed platform identities, initial installation receipts, and installed update checks remain pending.

features.title: An executable design system
features.description: Explore shared tokens, components, interaction states, and client specimens in a React/Vite review browser.
details: Review visual behavior and constrained layouts before production UI changes.
Keep native clients aligned with the written design authority.
features.note: Review tooling only. Web and TUI specimens do not mean those clients are implemented.

features.title: Harbor benchmark adapter
features.description: Run a supplied native CLI binary in Harbor / Terminal-Bench tasks and convert traces to ATIF format.
details: Retains JSONL and stderr artifacts for inspection.
Uses the ordinary CLI policy and tool boundary.
features.note: Separate benchmark tooling; it does not provision the CLI or establish a benchmark score, ranking, or performance claim.

features.title: The public product website
features.description: Explore SunCode's workflows and complete feature guide, and find the open-source implementation.
details: Server-rendered product pages with responsive navigation and searchable capability descriptions.
Hosts public update metadata with offline publication tooling.
features.note: This is a product information website, separate from the deferred Web agent client. Signed metadata is not proof of usable package downloads.
